questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line $y=m x$ bisects the area unclosed by lines $x=0, y=0$ and $x=\frac{3}{2}$ and the curve $y=1+4 x-x^2$. Then, the value of $m$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $y=1+4 x-x^2\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=4-2 x=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \text{[point$ of $maxima]}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad y_{\max }=1+4 \times 2-4=5
\end{aligned}$ when, $x=0, y=1\therefore$ Graph according to question and above information

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \text{ If } y=m x \text{ bisects the area bounded } \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A_1=A_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \int_0^{3 / 2}\left(1+4 x-x^2\right) d x=2 \int_0^{3 / 2} m x d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left[x+2 x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{3 / 2}=\left[m x^2\right]_0^{3 / 2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}+2 \times \frac{9}{4}-\frac{27}{8} \times \frac{1}{3}=m \times \frac{9}{4} \\ & \therefore \quad m=\frac{13}{6}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a, c, b$ are in GP, then the area of the triangle formed by the lines $a x+b y+c=0$ with the coordinates axes is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $a, c, b$ are in GP
$\Rightarrow \quad c^2=a b$...(i)
According to question,

$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \text{ Area of } \triangle O A B & =\left|\frac{1}{2} \times O A \times O B\right| \\
= & \left|\frac{1}{2} \times\left(\frac{-c}{b}\right) \times\left(\frac{-c}{a}\right)\right| \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{c^2}{a b}=\frac{1}{2} [by Eq. (i)]
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $y=x^3$ and $y=\sqrt{x}$ is
questions.solution:
Given curves are y=x^3 and $y=\sqrt{x}$
Both curves intersects at $x=0 and x=1$

Shaded region is required area
$\begin{aligned}
A & =\left|\int_0^1\left(x^3-\sqrt{x}\right) d x\right|=\left|\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{2 x^{3 / 2}}{3}\right]_0^1\right| \\
& =\left|\left[\frac{1}{4}-\frac{2}{3}\right]\right| \\
& =\frac{5}{12} \text{ sq. unit }
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $x=y^2-2$ and $x=y$ is
questions.solution: Given, $x=y^2-2 and x=y$. On solving, $x=y^2-2 and x=y$, we get $(-1,-1) and (2,2)$. Area of the shaded region, $\begin{aligned} & A=\int_{-1}^2 y d y-\int_{-1}^2\left(y^2-2\right) d y \\ & =\left[\frac{y^2}{2}-\frac{y^3}{3}+2 y\right]_{-1}^2=\left(\frac{4}{2}-\frac{8}{3}+4\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-2\right) \\ & =\frac{10}{3}+\frac{7}{6}=\frac{27}{6}=\frac{9}{2}. \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the area bounded by the curves $y=a x^2$ and $x=a y^2,(a>0)$ is 3 sq units, then the value of $a$ is
questions.solution: We have given, $y=a x^2$ ....(i) and $x=a y^2$ ......(ii) Put the value of $y$ by Eq. (i) in Eq. (ii), we get $x=a \times a^2 x^4 \Rightarrow x^4 a^3-x=0x\left(x^3 a^3-1\right)=0 \Rightarrow x=0, \frac{1}{2}$ When, $x=0 \Rightarrow y=0$ and $x=\frac{1}{a} \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{a}$ Here, points of intersection of curves $y=a x^2 and x=a y^2$ are (0,0) and $\left(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{a}\right)$. $\therefore \quad$ Required area $A=\int_{x=a}^{x=b}\left[f_2(x)-f_1(x)\right] d x3=\int_0^{1 / a}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{a}}-a x^2\right) d x3=\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} \times \frac{2}{3} x^{3 / 2}-\frac{a x^3}{3}\right]_0^{1 / a}3=\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{a}}\left[\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{3 / 2}\right]-\frac{a}{3}\left[\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^3\right]3=\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{a}} \times \frac{1}{a \sqrt{a}}-\frac{a}{3} \times \frac{1}{a^3}3=\frac{2}{3 a^2}-\frac{1}{3 a^2} \Rightarrow 3=\frac{2-1}{3 a^2} \Rightarrow 9 a^2=1a^2=\frac{1}{9} \Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.q: The area of the region$\mathbf{R}=\left\{(x, y): 5 x^2 \leq y \leq 2 x^2+9\right\} \text{$ is : }
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Required area }=2 \int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\left(2 x^2+9-5 x^2\right) d x \\ & =2\left[9 x-x^3\right]_0^{\sqrt{3}}=2[9 \sqrt{3}-3 \sqrt{3}]=12 \sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area enclosed between the curve $y=\log _e(x+e)$ and the coordinate axes is
questions.solution:
Required area $A=\int_{1-e}^0 y d x=\int_{1-e}^0 \log _e(x+e) d x$
put $x+e=t \Rightarrow d x=d t$ also when $x=1-e, t=$ 1 and when $x=0, t=e$
$\therefore A=\int_1^e \log _e t d t=\left[t \log _e t-t\right]_1^e$
$e-e-0+1=1$

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the parabola $(y-2)^2=(x-1)$, the tangent to the parabola at the point $(2,3)$ and the $X$-axis is
questions.solution: The equation of the parabola is $y^2-4 y-x+5=0$ The equation of tangent at $(2,3)$ is $\begin{aligned}$3 y-2(y+3)-$\frac{x+2}{2}+$5 & =0 \\ 2 y-x-4 & =0 \end{aligned} $$ \\ $\therefore$ Required area $A$ is given by $\begin{aligned}$& A=\int_0^3$\left($x_2-x_1\right) d y \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A=\int_0^3$\left[\left$\{(y-2)^2+1\right\}-\{2 y-4\}\right] d y \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A=\int_0^3$\left($y^2-6 y+9\right) d y=\int_0^3(3-y)^2 d y \\ & =-$\left[\frac{(3-y)^3}{3}\right]_$0^3=9 \\ & \end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $y=\sin x+\cos x$ and $y=|\cos x-\sin x|$ over the interval $\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $y=\sin x+\cos x, x \in[0, \pi / 2]\frac{d y}{d x}=\cos x-\sin x\begin{aligned} y & =|\cos x-\sin x| \\ & =\left[$\begin{array}{cc}$\cos x-\sin$ x & x \in[0, \pi / 4] \\ $\sin x-\cos$ x & x \in[\pi / 4, \pi / 2]\end{array}$\right]\end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Required area $\begin{aligned} &=\int_0^{\pi / 4}|(\sin x+\cos x)-(\cos x-\sin x)| d x+\int_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2}|2 \cos x| d x \end{aligned}=\int_0^{\pi / 4}|2 \sin x| d x+\int_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2}|2 \cos x| d x=2(-\cos x)_0^{\pi / 4}+2(\sin x)_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2}=2 \left[-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+1+1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]
\begin{aligned}=$& 2$\left(2-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$\\ = & 2(2-$\sqrt{2})$\\ = & 4-2 $\sqrt{2}$\\ = & 2 $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2}-1)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curves $x+2 y^{2}=0$ and $x+3 y^{2}=1$ is
questions.solution:
We have, $x+2 y^{2}=0\Rightarrow y^{2}=-\frac{x}{2} \ldots \text{ (i) }$ a parabola with vertex $(0,0)$ and $x+3 y^{2}=1\Rightarrow y^{2}=\frac{1-x}{3}=-\left(\frac{x-1}{3}\right) \ldots$ (ii), a parabola with vertex $(1,0)$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get $y=\pm 1$
$\mathrm{A}=\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\left(1-3 y^{2}\right)-\left(-2 y^{2}\right)\right) d y=2 \int_{0}^{1}\left(1-y^{2}\right) d y=2\left[y-\frac{y^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}=\frac{4}{3}$ sq.units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by curves $(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}=1$ and $x^{2}+y^{2}=1$ is
questions.solution:
Given circles are $x^{2}+y^{2}=1 \ldots$ (i) and $(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}=1 \ldots$ (ii) Centre of (i) is $\mathrm{O}(0,0)$ and radius $=1$
Both these circle are symmetrical about $x$-axis solving (i) and (ii), we get, $-2 x+1=0$ $\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{2}$ $\begin{array}{l} \text{ then } y^{2}=1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}=34 \\ \Rightarrow y=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \end{array}$ $\therefore$ The points of intersection are $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ and $\mathrm{Q}\left(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ It is clear from the figure that the shaded portion in region whose area is required. $\therefore$ Required area = area OQAPO $=2 \times$ area of the region OLAP $=2 \times($ area of the region $O L P O+$ area of $L A P L$ ) $=2\left[\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}} d x+\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1} \sqrt{1-x^{2}} \mathrm{dx}\right]$ $=2\left[\frac{(x-1) \sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}}}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(x-1)\right]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}+2\left[\frac{x \sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1} x\right]_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}$ $=-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)-\sin ^{-1}(-1)+0+\sin ^{-1}(1)-\left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)$ $=\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ sq. units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Area bounded by two branches of the curve $\left(y - x\right)2 = x^{3}$ and x = 1 is
questions.solution:
Given, curve is $\left(y - x\right)2 = x^{3}$

$⇒ y - x = \pm x\sqrt{x}$

$⇒ y = x \pm x\sqrt{x}$

$∴$ Area bounded $= \left|{∫}_{0}^{1}\left\{\left(x + x\sqrt{x}\right) - \left(x - x\sqrt{x}\right)\right\}dx\right|$

$= \left|2{∫}_{0}^{1}x^{3 / 2}dx\right| = \dfrac{4}{5}squnit$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region included between the curves ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {a}^{2}$ and $\sqrt{\left|x\right|} + \sqrt{\left|y\right|} = \sqrt{a}\left(a > 0\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given curves are

$\sqrt{\left|x\right|} + \sqrt{\left|y\right|} = \sqrt{a} . . . \left(i\right)$

and ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {a}^{2} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, required areas $= 4$[shaded area in the first quadrant]

$= 4\left[\dfrac{\pi{a}^{2}}{4} - {∫}_{0}^{a}{\left(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{x}\right)}^{2}dx\right]$  [from Eqs. (i) and (ii)]

$= 4\left[\dfrac{\pi{a}^{2}}{4} - {∫}_{0}^{a}\left(a + x - 2\sqrt{a}\sqrt{x}\right)dx\right]$

$= 4\dfrac{\pi{a}^{2}}{4} - 4{\left[ax + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{a}{x}^{3 / 2}\right]}_{0}^{a}$

$= \left(\pi - \dfrac{2}{3}\right){a}^{2}$ sq units

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area under the curve $y = \left|cosx - sinx\right|, 0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and above $X$-axis, is
questions.solution:
Required area $= {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left|cosx - sinx\right|dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 4}\left(cosx - sinx\right)dx + {∫}_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2}\left(sinx - cosx\right)dx$

$= {sinx + cosx}_{0}^{\pi / 4} + {- cosx - sinx}_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2}$

$= \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right) - \left(1 - \sqrt{2}\right) = 2\sqrt{2} - 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A wire $34 \mathrm{ cm}$ long is to be bent in the form of a quadrilateral of which each angle is $90^{{}^{\circ}}.$ What is the maximum area which can be enclosed inside the quadrilateral?
questions.solution: Let one side of quadrilateral be $\mathrm{x}$ and another side be $y$ so, $2(x+y)=34$ or $(x+y)=17$ We know from the basic principle that for a given perimeter square has the maximum area, $\mathrm{so}, \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y}$ and putting this value in equation (i) $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y}=\frac{17}{2}$ Area $=x \cdot y=\frac{17}{2} \times \frac{17}{2}=\frac{289}{4}=72.25$

questions.solution: Required area $=4$ (Area of the shaded region in first quadrant) =4 \int_{0}^{1 $\sqrt{2}}\left($ y_{1}-y_{2}\right) d x=4 \int_{0}^{1 $\sqrt{2}}\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}-$ x\right) d x $=4\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{1-x^{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1} x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1 / \sqrt{2}}=4\left[\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\right]=4\left[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac{1}{4}\right]=\frac{4 \pi}{8}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ sq units

questions.q: The area bounded by the $x$ -axis, the curve $y=f(x)$ and the lines $\mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{b},$ is equal to $\sqrt{\mathrmb^{2}+1}-\sqrt{2}$ for all $b > 1,$ then $f(x)$ is
questions.solution: Given $\int_{1}^{\mathrm{b}} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{dx}=\sqrt{\mathrmb^{2}+1}-\sqrt{2}$ Differentiate with respect to $\mathrm{b}$ f(b)=$\frac{b}{\sqrt{b^{2}+1}} \Rightarrow$ f(x)=$\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}$
